verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere ships explicit SDKs for Swift and Kotlin and touts a shared C++ core with 'six thin bindings' that also covers a React Native (JavaScript) integration for on-device LLM/STT/TTS, and its Wally Cloud endpoint is OpenAI-compatible so official OpenAI Python/JS client libraries can call it by setting base_url. However there is no explicit doc naming a first-party Python SDK, and the JS/TS binding's API surface is only inferred from the React Native integration guide rather than documented directly like Swift/Kotlin. Missing for 10: a dedicated Python client library, explicit JS/TS SDK API reference (not just an Expo integration guide), and independent confirmation that these bindings work end-to-end.
